name: Barnes Foundation
unique: Dr. Barnes collected 181 Renoirs, 69 Cezannes and 59 Matisses and hung them in ensembles meant to teach visual thinking, now in a Tod Williams building on the Parkway.
buzz: The hang is the lesson and people either love or fight it; book a timed ticket and give it three hours, the collection is denser than it looks.

name: Philadelphia's Magic Gardens
customer: Mosaic people, photographers, South Street wanderers
unique: Half a block of South Street tiled by Isaiah Zagar with bottles, mirrors, bicycle wheels and folk art, with a basement grotto you crawl through.
buzz: People come for a photo and stay for the story of the neighborhood; the outdoor lot needs a ticket and the surrounding alleys are free.

name: Italian Market
unique: Nine blocks of 9th Street where cheesemakers, butchers and tortilla factories still work behind open counters, with the Philadelphia side of the market running since the 1880s.
buzz: Go on a weekday morning and start at the top; the weekend crowd is a wall and the produce prices are the best in the city.

name: Andy Warhol Museum
unique: Seven floors holding 900 paintings, the Silver Clouds room and Warhol's time capsules, in the industrial building on the North Shore where he was born a few miles away.
buzz: The top floor films and the cloud room are the ones people remember; the permanent collection is so deep that a second visit is different.

name: Duquesne Incline
company: Society for the Preservation of the Duquesne Heights Incline
unique: A wooden 1877 funicular up Mount Washington, still run by hand by a operator in the upper station, ending at the three rivers view that defines the city.
buzz: Ride up at dusk and walk down the steps or take it back; the upper station has a small museum of the machinery and the fare is cash friendly.

name: Phipps Conservatory
unique: A Victorian glasshouse in Schenley Park with a tropical forest under glass, a butterfly room and a Center for Sustainable Landscapes that is one of the greenest buildings in the world.
buzz: The winter flower show is the local tradition and the summer butterfly room is the family draw; the glasshouse is hot in July.

name: Kennywood
unique: A trolley park from 1898 with three wooden coasters, a 1920s Noah's Ark walkthrough and the Thunderbolt, all on a bluff above the Monongahela.
buzz: Coaster people rank the Phantom's Revenge and the Jack Rabbit; the park is small enough that a day pass covers everything twice.

name: Lancaster Central Market
unique: The oldest continuously operating farmers market in the country, in a brick hall where Amish farm stands sell scrapple, chow chow and whoopie pies beside Lebanese and Jamaican counters.
buzz: Saturday is the crush and Tuesday is the locals; the smoked meats and the pretzels are the standing orders and cash is still normal.

name: Strasburg Rail Road
unique: The oldest short line railroad in the country, running a steam locomotive 45 minutes through Amish farm fields from a 1830s depot.
buzz: Book the open air car and sit on the left; children want the steam engine and the shop sells the wooden version for the ride home.

name: Amish Farm and House
customer: Families, first time visitors, school groups
unique: A 1805 farmhouse and working farm where a guide explains Amish schooling, barn raising and plain dress, with a bus tour into the back roads.
buzz: The house tour is better than the bus for understanding the religion; visitors say the guides answer the awkward questions honestly.

name: Harley-Davidson York Factory Tour
customer: Motorcycle people, engineers, families with teens
unique: The plant where every Harley frame and fuel tank is made and painted, walked on a catwalk above the assembly line with closed toe shoes required.
buzz: Riders call it a pilgrimage and non riders are surprised by the robots; tours fill weeks out and the plant shuts in some holiday weeks.

name: York Central Market
unique: A two story brick market house with a balcony of lunch counters, where York's German farm stands became Pennsylvania Dutch lunch stands over 130 years.
buzz: The pretzel and the chicken corn soup are the orders; it is smaller than Lancaster's and easier to actually shop.

name: Pennsylvania State Capitol
customer: Architecture people, school groups, statehouse collectors
unique: A Beaux Arts capitol Roosevelt called the handsomest in the nation, with a 272 foot dome, Moravian tiles and a limestone staircase modeled on the Paris opera.
buzz: The free tour is the only way into the rotunda and the House chamber; the tile work is what visitors photograph.

name: National Civil War Museum
unique: A hilltop museum that tells the war from both sides with a balance rare among Civil War sites, from the 1850s causes through reconstruction, with a large collection of soldiers' letters.
buzz: Visitors say it is the honest overview the battlefields do not give; the walk up the hill is steep and the view over Harrisburg is the bonus.

name: Broad Street Market
unique: Two brick market houses from the Civil War era, one of the oldest continuously operating markets in the country, with Pennsylvania Dutch stands and a growing row of Syrian and Vietnamese counters.
buzz: The stone building is the food hall and the brick building is the produce; go hungry and expect a line at the sandwich stands.

name: US Army Heritage and Education Center
unique: A free army museum with a mile long outdoor trail of reproduced fortifications from the French and Indian War to Vietnam, plus a research library of soldiers' letters.
buzz: The outdoor heritage trail is the surprise and you can walk inside a bunker and a trench; the indoor galleries are small and rotate.

name: Appalachian Trail Museum
unique: The only museum devoted to the Appalachian Trail, in an 1820s ironmaster's mansion where thru hikers still stop for a bunk, with packs, boots and journals from the trail.
buzz: Thru hikers sign the register and volunteers feed them; in June the porch is full of people who walked from Georgia.

name: Dorney Park
unique: A 1884 trolley park with a 1920s carousel, a steel hypercoaster and a water park on the same ticket, in the hills above Allentown.
buzz: The water park is the summer value and the coasters are the reason enthusiasts come; weekdays in June are empty enough to loop everything.

name: America on Wheels Museum
customer: Car and truck people, families, dads
unique: A transportation museum on the Lehigh River with a Mack truck gallery, a 1950s gas station and a rotating exhibit of cars you can walk around and under.
buzz: The truck room is what makes it different from every car museum; it is small and the admission is cheap enough for a rainy hour.

name: SteelStacks
unique: The Bethlehem Steel plant turned arts campus, where the blast furnaces stand lit at night above a lawn that hosts free summer concerts and a film series.
buzz: The furnaces at night are the photograph everyone takes; the free Levitt Pavilion shows are the local summer ritual.

name: National Museum of Industrial History
unique: A Smithsonian affiliate in a former Bethlehem Steel building, with a working steam engine, the only remaining screw propeller from the Titanic's sister ship and a silk loom you can run.
buzz: The volunteers start the engines and talk forever; the machine shop is the best part and children can operate several exhibits.

name: Crayola Experience
unique: The crayon factory's visitor center where children name and wrap their own crayon, mold wax and watch how a crayon is made, in the town where Crayola began.
buzz: Parents say three hours is the limit and the meltdown happens at the gift shop; buy tickets online and go at opening.

name: Steamtown National Historic Site
unique: A working rail yard in the old Lackawanna shops with a roundhouse, a turntable you can watch turn a locomotive and short steam excursions through the valley.
buzz: Train people spend all day and families do the roundhouse and the short ride; check the excursion schedule before going.

name: Lackawanna Coal Mine Tour
unique: A mine car drops you 300 feet into a anthracite seam where a former miner explains the work at a temperature of 53 degrees year round.
buzz: The guides are retired miners and the stories are the tour; bring a jacket and expect to duck, the seam is low.

name: Houdini Museum
customer: Magic fans, families, curious road trippers
unique: A magic museum and theater in a Scranton house where a working magician gives a tour of Houdini's handcuffs and escape trunks, then performs a show.
buzz: It is part museum and part vaudeville and children are the right audience; the tour and show run as one ticket.

name: Bushkill Falls
unique: Eight waterfalls on a privately owned gorge with boardwalks and stairs, the tallest dropping 100 feet, reached by a mile of trail in the Poconos.
buzz: The red trail covers everything and takes two hours; it is a paid attraction, which people either resent or appreciate for the upkeep.

name: Delaware Water Gap
unique: The river cuts through the Kittatinny Ridge at a notch you can climb above on the Appalachian Trail, with a beach, a canoe launch and a view of New Jersey from the top.
buzz: The Mount Tammany red dot trail is steep and crowded and the reward is the gap from above; the river beach is the easy alternative.

name: Pocono Raceway
unique: A triangle shaped superspeedway where you can camp inside the infield, watch three turns at once and see the cars come at you down the long front stretch.
buzz: The infield camping is the experience and the traffic afterwards is the warning; the July race is the big one.

name: Presque Isle State Park
company: Pennsylvania Department of Conservation and Natural Resources
unique: A seven mile sand spit curving into Lake Erie with eleven beaches, a flat multi use trail and a lagoon where migrating birds pile up in spring.
buzz: Sunsets over the bay side are the local ritual; the peninsula trail is flat and the beaches get crowded only in July.

name: Erie Maritime Museum
unique: The home port of the Brig Niagara, Perry's reconstructed flagship from the Battle of Lake Erie, with a museum on the 1813 battle and a winter shipyard you can watch.
buzz: Sailing on the Niagara is the splurge and books out; the museum alone explains why a freshwater lake had a naval war.

name: Waldameer Park
unique: A trolley era park with a 1908 carousel, a wooden coaster and a water park, free to enter so you can walk the midway without buying a ride wristband.
buzz: Locals love that admission is free and parking is cheap; the Ravine Flyer II is the coaster enthusiasts come for.
